extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of classical Euclidean geometry (advanced high-school / undergraduate level)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted propositions, problems and theorems from Euclid's Elements, Book VI: geometric statements about similar figures, proportionality, constructions (cutting/dividing lines, finding proportional/mean/third/fourth proportionals), and relations between areas/rectangles in proportion. Includes construction methods and corollaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. A. THEOR. (outward angle / base produced ratio)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the outward angle of a triangle, made by producing one of its sides, be divided into two equal angles by a straight line which also cuts the base produced; the segments between the dividing line and the extremities of the base have the same ratio which the other sides of the triangle have to one another. Conversely, if the segments of the base produced have the same ratio which the other sides of the triangle have, the straight line drawn from the vertex to the point of section divides the outward angle into two equal angles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: draw a line through the opposite vertex parallel to the bisecting line, use alternate and corresponding angles to show equal triangles or equal sides, then deduce proportionality. Conversely, assume proportionality of base segments, join vertex to section, show equal corresponding sides then deduce equal angles. (Proof uses parallels, alternate interior angles, and equality of sides leading to equal angles.)

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. IV. THEOR. (sides about equal angles are proportional)
rubrics_metrics.description: The sides about the equal angles of equiangular triangles are proportionals; and those which are opposite to the equal angles are homologous sides, i.e., are the antecedents or consequents of the ratios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given two equiangular triangles place one so a side is contiguous to the other, show certain lines are parallel, produce a parallelogram to identify equal segments, and use proportionality relations (alternation/composition) to deduce the proportionality of sides about equal angles and identify homologous sides. (Proof uses parallel lines, parallelogram properties, and alternation of ratios.)

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. V. THEOR. (proportional sides ⇒ triangles equiangular)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the sides of two triangles, about each of their angles, be proportionals, the triangles shall be equiangular, and have their equal angles opposite to the homologous sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct a triangle with equal angles at chosen points and use proportionality to prove corresponding sides equal, then deduce that corresponding angles are equal. The proof uses making equal angles on a line and comparing triangles via side proportions leading to equality of sides and hence equality of angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. VI. THEOR. (one equal angle + proportional adjacent sides ⇒ triangles equiangular)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two triangles have one angle of the one equal to one angle of the other, and the sides about the equal angles proportionals, the triangles shall be equiangular, and shall have those angles equal which are opposite to the homologous sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct auxiliary triangle(s) replicating angles on a common line, use proportionality and equality to show side-equalities and hence equality of remaining angles. Uses alternation of ratios and equal-triangle arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. VII. THEOR. (one equal angle + proportional sides about two other angles ⇒ equiangular under angle-size conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two triangles have one angle of the one equal to one angle of the other, and the sides about two other angles proportionals, then, if each of the remaining angles be either less, or not less, than a right angle; or if one of them be a right angle: the triangles shall be equiangular, and have those angles equal about which the sides are proportionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof proceeds by contradiction: assume the corresponding angles unequal, construct auxiliary angles equal to one triangle's angle, use the proportionality hypothesis to force equal segments and obtain contradictions with angle size assumptions (less/greater/right). The proposition handles three cases (both remaining angles less than right, both not less than right, or one a right angle).

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. VIII. THEOR. (right triangle altitude ⇒ similar triangles)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a right-angled triangle, if a perpendicular be drawn from the right angle to the base, the triangles on each side of it are similar to the whole triangle, and to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use right angles and shared angles to show equiangularity; consequently the perpendicular from the right angle to the base is a mean proportional between the base segments, and each side is a mean proportional between the whole base and the adjacent base-segment. (Corollary explicitly states the mean-proportional relations and the ratio equalities among sides and segments.)

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. IX. PROB. (cut off any required part from a given line)
rubrics_metrics.description: From a given straight line to cut off any part required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: from one endpoint draw an arbitrary line, mark a segment on it proportional to the desired fraction, join and draw a parallel to cut off the requested part. Proof relies on parallels producing equal ratios; uses composition of ratios to verify the part is the required proportion of the whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. X. PROB. (divide a line similarly to a given divided line)
rubrics_metrics.description: To divide a given straight line similarly to a given divided straight line, i.e., into parts that shall have the same ratios to one another which the parts of the divided given straight line have.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the two lines to form an angle, through division points draw parallels, then use parallelogram and parallel-line proportionality arguments to transfer the ratios, showing the given line is divided in the same proportions. (Construction uses drawing parallels at corresponding division points.)

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XI. PROB. (find a third proportional to two given lines)
rubrics_metrics.description: To find a third proportional to two given straight lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the two lines forming an angle, extend both, make a segment equal to the second on the extension of the first, draw a line and construct a parallel so that the resulting segment is the third proportional. Proof uses parallelism to obtain AB:AC :: AC:CE.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XII. PROB. (find a fourth proportional to three given lines)
rubrics_metrics.description: To find a fourth proportional to three given straight lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On two lines forming an angle construct segments equal to the given first three lines consecutively, join two of them and draw a parallel through the middle point to produce a segment HF such that A:B :: C:HF. Uses parallels and proportionality of sides of similar triangles.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XIII. PROB. (find a mean proportional between two given lines)
rubrics_metrics.description: To find a mean proportional between two given straight lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the two segments as parts of a straight line, construct a semicircle on the whole, drop a perpendicular from the junction point to the semicircle; that perpendicular is the mean proportional between the two given segments. Uses the right-angle-in-semicircle fact and Prop. VIII about mean proportionals from an altitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XIV. THEOR. (equal parallelograms with one equal angle ⇒ reciprocally proportional sides)
rubrics_metrics.description: Equal parallelograms which have one angle of the one equal to one angle of the other, have their sides about the equal angles reciprocally proportional; and parallelograms that have one angle of the one equal to one angle of the other, and their sides about the equal angles reciprocally proportional, are equal to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place sides on a straight line, complete a third parallelogram and use properties of equal parallelograms and reciprocal proportionality of adjacent sides to deduce equalities. The converse is proved similarly by constructing parallelograms and using reciprocal ratios to show equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XV. THEOR. (equal triangles with one equal angle ⇒ reciprocally proportional adjacent sides)
rubrics_metrics.description: Equal triangles which have one angle of the one equal to one angle of the other, have their sides about the equal angles reciprocally proportional; and triangles which have one angle in the one equal to one angle in the other, and their sides about the equal angles reciprocally proportional, are equal to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the triangles so corresponding sides lie on a line and join vertices; use ratios of triangle areas/sides and equal-triangle arguments to derive reciprocal proportionality. Converse: from reciprocal proportionality deduce triangle equality via ratio-of-triangles arguments and side equalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XVI. THEOR. (four proportionals ⇒ rectangle of extremes = rectangle of means)
rubrics_metrics.description: If four straight lines be proportionals (AB:CD :: E:F), the rectangle contained by the extremes is equal to the rectangle contained by the means; and if the rectangle contained by the extremes be equal to the rectangle contained by the means, the four straight lines are proportionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct perpendiculars equal to the appropriate lengths and complete parallelograms; use earlier proposition about equal parallelograms with reciprocal sides to deduce equality of rectangles and conversely deduce proportionality from rectangle equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XVII. THEOR. (three proportionals ⇒ rectangle of extremes = square of mean)
rubrics_metrics.description: If three straight lines be proportionals (A:B :: B:C), the rectangle contained by the extremes is equal to the square of the mean; and if the rectangle contained by the extremes be equal to the square of the mean, the three straight lines are proportionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to the four-proportional case by duplicating the mean and applying Prop. XVI; uses equality of rectangles and squares and previous proportionality results to prove both directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XVIII. PROB. (describe a rectilineal figure similar and similarly situated to a given one on a given line)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon a given straight line to describe a rectilineal figure similar, and similarly situated to a given rectilineal figure (of four or more sides).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct triangles equiangular to corresponding triangles of the given figure by making equal angles at endpoints of the given base, then continue for subsequent sides by making corresponding angles equal and using equiangular triangle similarity to ensure sides about equal angles are proportional, yielding a similar and similarly situated polygon. Extend method iteratively for polygons with more sides.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XIX. THEOR. (similar triangles have duplicate ratio of homologous sides)
rubrics_metrics.description: Similar triangles are to one another in the duplicate ratio of their homologous sides: if AB:BC :: DE:EF (BC homologous to EF), then triangle ABC : triangle DEF is the duplicate ratio of BC : EF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take a third proportional BG to BC:EF so BC:EF :: EF:BG, form triangle ABG and show ABG is equal to DEF via reciprocity of adjacent sides; then use the notion that if three lines are proportionals, the first has to the third the duplicate ratio of the first to the second, and relate triangle ratios to side ratios to conclude the duplicate ratio claim. Corollary: triangles on proportional sides have corresponding duplicate area/similarity scaling consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XX. THEOR. (similar polygons divided into similar triangles; duplicate ratio of homologous sides)
rubrics_metrics.description: Similar polygons may be divided into the same number of similar triangles, having the same ratio to one another that the polygons have; and the polygons have to one another the duplicate ratio of that which their homologous sides have.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divide polygons by diagonals from a chosen vertex into triangles; prove corresponding triangles are pairwise similar using equiangular and proportional-side arguments; deduce each corresponding triangle pair has the same ratio as the polygons, and the polygon-to-polygon ratio is the duplicate ratio of a homologous side-to-side ratio. (Uses prior triangle-similarity and duplicate-ratio results.)
